[quote=the_crystalline_empire;60620095]"Well as you know we already have a carrier force in the White Strait about 70 miles from the coast of Tallisland with a combined force of around 8,000 men, plus another carrier fleet on standby back in the Free Republic of Knygta and Deyn. Now the Neue Republik has made it clear that they will not accept any strike against Tallisland, who happens to be also a member of the EDU, though, their position in the eyes of the government of Thýven is laughable. Albeit your forces seem to be more strategically ground oriented whereas we rely heavily on naval and aerial matters for our war doctrine, if we can combine our efforts we would have an excellent trio of aerial, ground, and naval forces readied and active to ensure the stability of the state of Tallisland," He paused before continuing, lowering his voice slightly, "There is little doubt that before the end of 2026 or even early 2027, Thýven intends to blow a few holes in the ego's at the government offices in the Neue Republik,"[/quote]

"Well, that's great. Im glad we seemingly have the same goals here, even if for different reasons. And yes, due to our...lack of a navy, we are mostly ground-oriented. I think there is something we could do that would greatly improve our strategic position in Tallisland in that regard."

He pulls out a map of the island chain in the white sea, which Tallisland owns.

"Fuelenger suggested to me earlier that securing these islands, almost dead center in the white sea, could be a good position to further aid Tallisland from, especially if we could secure intact airports so we could airlift troops and supplies more easily from those islands to the mainland. We would need your navy to secure the waters around the island. But according to Fuelenger, it wouldn't be hard to then secure the island through an amphibious landing"

He thinks for another second before continuing

"Speaking of navies, your navy is free to dock in Komend if needed for resupply in fuel and ammunition. If you airlift the munitions here beforehand, our dockworkers would be more than capable of loading them for you, which would be much faster than sailing all the way back to your country."
